text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis

The description of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand of a sun-exposed 65-year-old with a history of diabetes is clinically consistent with Actinic Keratosis. The lack of pain or tenderness supports a benign, pre-malignant etiology rather than an infectious process like a cellulitis or an acute infection unrelated to the skin surface. Given your age and sun exposure history, we should proceed with a biopsy to rule out early squamous cell carcinoma.
